hunt.justification: The AD RMS SLC key is the master root for all organizationally protected data. Its extraction allows permanent, offline decryption that is undetectable post-extraction and persists across infrastructure rebuilds. Confirming it is secure is a top-tier data protection priority.

meta.name: AD RMS Root Key Discovery and Extraction

related.reason: This hunt focuses on server-side root key extraction; client-side protection stripping (DisARMS) is a separate threat.

meta.analysis: A standard rule may flag the SharpRMS binary, but this hunt pivots between infrastructure discovery (SQL/RMS server identification), behavioral command analysis (keyprotection), fleet-wide tool prevalence, and anomalous sign-ins to confirm a root key theft across several telemetry surfaces.

stages.name: Compromise of AD RMS Service Group Account
RMS Service and Key Configuration Recon

scenario.summary: An attacker compromises a privileged AD RMS Service Group account to discover protected documents and configuration details. By extracting the 255-year-valid Server Licensor Certificate (SLC) private key via SOAP export or direct SQL database access, the attacker gains the ability to decrypt every document ever protected by the deployment offline.

meta.rationale: Start by identifying the AD RMS cluster nodes and the SQL database server. Analysis of process and auth logs should focus on these high-value targets identified in the first query.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has compromised an AD RMS Service Group account to discover configuration (software-backed keys) and extract the SLC private key via TPD export or direct SQL access.

blind_spots.risk: An attacker can sweep shares for RMS-protected files without detection if only path-level telemetry is available.
blind_spots.question: whether a process is specifically searching for the D0-CF OLE magic or RMS streams
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy file scanning solutions that report on OLE compound file streams in transit.

blind_spots.risk: Legitimate admin activity and malicious extraction use the same SOAP surface; without payload visibility, detection relies on process and account anomalies.
blind_spots.question: the specific SOAP method (e.g., TPD export) being invoked over HTTPS
blind_spots.requires: HTTPS decryption or AD RMS server-side audit logs
blind_spots.remediation: Enable AD RMS administrative SOAP logging to capture export events.

hunt.name: AD RMS Root Key Discovery and Extraction
hunt.description: This hunt targets the critical extraction of the AD RMS Server Licensor Certificate (SLC) private key. This 255-year root key allows for permanent, offline decryption of all documents protected by the cluster. The hunt identifies the execution of discovery tools like SharpRMS and the 'keyprotection' command, assesses the prevalence of these tools across the fleet, and corroborates with anomalous logins and unusual web traffic to the RMS administrative SOAP surface. By targeting the servers identified during infrastructure scoping, it avoids broad detection noise and focuses on high-impact administrative bypasses.

nodes.label: Detection of RMS Recon and Extraction Tools

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%keyprotection%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sharprms%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%tpdexport%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find execution of the 'keyprotection' command or SharpRMS tool used to find and extract root keys.
config.expected_signal: Evidence of an operator querying the RMS service configuration for software-based keys or performing a TPD export. Promoted to a rule if consistent.

primitive_config.label: Detection of RMS Recon and Extraction Tools
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%keyprotection%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sharprms%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%tpdexport%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
primitive_config.expected: Evidence of an operator querying the RMS service configuration for software-based keys or performing a TPD export. Promoted to a rule if consistent.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS tool, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, COUNT(*) AS run_count, MIN(time) AS first_run FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%keyprotection%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sharprms%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY tool HAVING host_count < 5 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Stack-count specific RMS configuration tools to identify rare/unauthorized usage across the estate.
config.expected_signal: Rare tools appearing on only one or two hosts, potentially indicating lateral movement or unauthorized admin activity.

primitive_config.label: Prevalence of RMS Configuration Tools
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_name) AS tool, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, COUNT(*) AS run_count, MIN(time) AS first_run FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%keyprotection%' OR LOWER(process_cmd_line) LIKE '%sharprms%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY tool HAVING host_count < 5 ORDER BY host_count ASC
primitive_config.expected: Rare tools appearing on only one or two hosts, potentially indicating lateral movement or unauthorized admin activity.

config.objective: Determine if the AD RMS root key (SLC) has been extracted by correlating 'keyprotection' discovery commands, rare tooling prevalence, and non-browser web traffic to the RMS servers.
config.description: Analyze the overlap of scoping, commands, prevalence, auth, and network activity to determine if a root key extraction occurred.
config.expected_signal: A verdict citing specific hosts where discovery followed by extraction traffic is observed.
config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign per host, citing the overlap of tools and traffic.

config.question: The triage verdict is malicious for an extraction attempt using SharpRMS or TPD export patterns targeting identified infrastructure.
config.condition: The triage verdict is malicious for an extraction attempt using SharpRMS or TPD export patterns targeting identified infrastructure.
config.description: Route the hunt to isolation or manual review based on the triage agent's findings.
Prevent further extraction or use of the stolen SLC key material.
config.instructions: Isolate the compromised RMS/SQL server immediately. Revoke the credentials for any compromised account identified in the triage. Begin forensic recovery and SLC key audit.

config.description: Review findings where the agent was undecided or data was unavailable.
config.instructions: Manually inspect the process and network events on the flagged hosts. Check database audit logs if available for direct table access to SLC keys on the SQL backend.

config.description: Finalize the hunt and document the security posture.
config.instructions: Document the hosts examined. If software-based keys are confirmed but no extraction occurred, recommend the infrastructure team move the SLC to an HSM.
